resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT actually a dead link — the current_ref returns HTTP 200 and is a live 17-page project-status report from Iraq's State Company for Oil Projects (شركة المشاريع النفطية / SCOP), Ministry of Oil, dated 2025-05-20. The automated verifier's initial FAIL was a false negative: it can't match contiguous Arabic substrings in this scanned/ligature-encoded PDF (English tokens like 'Karbala'/'gas' obviously don't appear in an Arabic doc). Manual pdftotext -layout extraction confirms the exact project on row 11 of the projects table: 'عقد تنفيذ مد انبوب الغاز الجاف 18 عقدة المغذي لمحطة كهرباء كربلاء الغازية' = 'execution contract for laying the 18-inch dry-gas pipeline feeding the Karbala gas power plant', executed by SCOP, cost ~4,000m IQD, planned completion 100% / actual completion 0% (i.e. contracted and in the execution/construction phase). It sits under the section header 'محطات الكهرباء الغازية الجديدة (حلة، كربلاء، تاجي)' = 'new gas power plants (Hilla, Karbala, Taji)'. This directly corroborates every GEM field: gas pipeline, 18-inch diameter, location Karbala, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil, and Status=construction (a signed execution/تنفيذ contract). The verifier returns OK when passed the token '18' (live, 200). Tier=medium because this is a single — though official, primary-source, government — document; despite extensive Arabic + English open-web searching I found no second independent source that names this specific Karbala 18-inch gas feeder line (open-web coverage names the sibling SCOP feeder lines — Kirkuk 16in, Diwaniya 24in, Bismaya/Basra 42in, Samawa 8in — and separately documents the Karbala gas power plant itself as under construction targeting summer-2026 trial operation, e.g. attaqa.net 2026-02-15, but none describe the pipeline). Note the separate Karbala Khairat thermal plant is fed by a 14-inch CRUDE line — not this project. Kept the original ref; it re-verifies.
